summary: Iranian IRGC drone strike on a Hormuz cargo vessel overnight reversed the oil normalization thesis — XLE short closed as thesis_broken (near-breakeven), UAL long hit Target 1 at +13.1%, META short hit Target 1 at +9.7%, MSFT long stopped out at -6.1% on sub-$360 close. Three new ideas added: tactical NVDA reconstitution long (1-2 days, mechanical passive bid), short QQQ into quarter-end/reconstitution volatility, and short AAPL on DRAM-driven hardware price increases. Regime stays STEP ASIDE — Brent $74.43 (+2.66% overnight), VIX 18.89, SPX 138 pts below 7,460 floor, BTC exit gate Day 3 active at $59,419.

closed_today.note: Hormuz drone strike June 25 directly inverted the normalization premise. Iran demanded transit fees; IMO paused evacuation plan; Brent spiked from $72.50 to $74.43. The XLE short thesis required sustained Hormuz normalization driving Brent toward $65 — thesis inverted overnight. Briefing called for exit at open June 26. Position closed at approximately breakeven (-0.9% from $56.0 reference).

UAL reached $134.37 on June 26 (range $130.54–$138.44), clearing Target 1 at $128. Fuel-cost relief from WTI declining from conflict-peak ~$90 toward $74–78 drove the move. Target 1 hit and exceeded before the Hormuz re-escalation risk became material. Position closed at +13.1% from $118.80 reference entry.

META declined from $602.45 reference to $544.19, clearing Target 1 at $555. EU DSA enforcement escalation, AI capex scrutiny, and Warsh FOMC 9-hike path compressed the multiple. The $555 target was exceeded by approximately $11. Short closed at +9.7%.

MSFT closed at $355.66 on June 25, below the $360 daily-close stop. Multiple headwinds: Warsh FOMC 9-hike path, Xbox hardware price increase, OpenAI IPO delay to 2027 removing near-term AI monetization catalyst. Stop triggered at -6.1% from $378.91 reference.
